video: Windows System Monitor: a real model, under the hood
notes: Rows are shown by the recorder's scenes (record.spec.ts). Rows with "on" wait for a captured event: a step of the assistant's run (GET /api/ai/runs/{id}), the run's start or its end.
Payloads come only from the capture (events.json); cues.mjs checks them. Callouts are [file, symbol], resolved by lines.mjs at take time.
Flexible mode: a real model's steps vary; a row that never matched is listed in take.json, and unforeseen tool calls get at most VIDEO_MAX_GENERIC generic rows.
B4 F1: Explain runs on the critical budget incident (numbers to check, a runbook); the Notepad scene shows a monitor opening one incident.

rows.subtitle: Windows System Monitor: the monitors decide; a small model on this PC explains.
One JSON file is the source of truth: what to watch, the thresholds, the actions and the runbooks.
Five monitors run on their own and write state files; the console only reads them.
The recorder closes Notepad. The process monitor notices on its next check.
One incident opens, with its start time and level: one incident, not a stream of alerts.
Explain the critical one: a small model on this PC, with four tools that can only read.
It reads the incident: the value, the threshold, since when, and whether the monitor is alive.
Then the runbook the operator wrote for this alert.
And the latest log lines about this item.
The model answered before reading, so the console read the data and asked again: no guess gets through.
Every number in the answer is checked against what the tools returned.
The same budget alert opened a ticket. Its priority comes from the rules.
Draft with AI: the model writes the description and the work notes.
The model writes the text; the code sets the priority, impact and urgency.
The email is only a draft: nothing is sent until you open it in your mail app.
Monitor data is data, never instructions: 21 scenarios, injection included, failures published.
Windows System Monitor. The monitors decide; the AI explains.
